[spoiler=[b]Operation Crusader[/b]]

Prior to the beginning of stage one of Operation Wailord, the HDF would greenlight Operation Crusader with the purpose of targeting the leadership of the Rosenmarkket armed forces and security apparatus. The core of the operation would be built around air launched ballistic missiles to utilize their high speed to quickly strike the leadership to give little time to react while also attempting to breach air defenses. B-1Bs carrying the Reichsadler ALBMs fire from stand-off ranges nearly 600 kilometers away from Rosenmarkke airspace from both the south in Wuloosya and the north in Corzerran. Using the combination of constant observation through SIGINT assets such as the RC-135, saturated aperture radar, AU-11J stealth observation drones and electro-optical satellites the HDF informed the location of various strikes. Travelling at a top speed of mach 10, the missiles quickly close in with their targets including the National State House, the Laakwujn Country Club, Jules Viernes Place, bunkers and command centers around the country. Arriving within 3-5 minutes of being launched from the bombers, the missiles limit reaction time for those targeted and air defenses. 

Shortly afterward, the decapitation strike would be followed by a mass saturation attack by the HDF against Rosenmarkket military infrastructure. Using a wave of 800 KV-5M expendable one-way attack drones and over 200 FAMM Barracuda-500 cruise missiles dropped from rapid dragon cells, air bases, runways, fuel supplies and portions of the electrical grid used to sustain military or strategic operations are targeted. 164 Tomahawk cruise missiles join the wave as the Donau-Klasse SSGN rises and quickly submerges again. Hyperschallsystem-5 ground based hypersonic weapons join the WDFs attack as stage one begins. Travelling at mach 8, the Republiks hypersonic glide vehicles join Wuloosya in attacking carriers and other high-value surface vessels. DF-26B anti-carrier missiles are fired off from their positions within Wuloosya. At its terminal stage the ballistic missiles travel at mach 10+ towards Rosenmarkket carriers, utilizing a maneuverable reentry vehicle to increase the accuracy of its strikes and avoid interception. 

As the strike is carried out, the JA-35s and their Vectis CCAs are at work suppressing and monitoring Rosenmarkke's air defense systems. As the fifth generations remain back, the CCAs help to continually suppress defenses. Should the Rosenmarkket air defenses activate to intercept the incoming Operation Wailord and Operation Crusader missiles the JA-35s and Vectis would fire off their AARGM-ER anti-radiation missiles. Joining the KV-5M drones are Peretz-Harris Negev loitering munitions. These drones aid the suppression mission by continually loitering until detecting a radar signature and then diving onto it. MALD drones are deployed again from J-16Cs with the dual purpose of creating further false targets and jamming Rosenmarkke communications to derail and mislead interception attempts. During the attack, EA-18G carrier-launched aircraft continually jam Rosenmarkket communications while working to spoof air defense systems with false targets.

By this time, around 70,000 members of the Hochdeutsche Armee and Marineinfantrie of the HDF would be deployed to Wuloosya marking the buildup of a major ground force in the region. Along with their LTAMDS air defense systems, ACVs, howitzers, artillery, NSMs and other equipment the force is meant to act as a deterrent against THEP and aid in future operations.[/spoiler]

[quote=nordiheim;61428448][spoiler=First F-130 purchase and a request for landing.]
[b]First order of F-130s[/b]

With the Joint-Initiative Aircraft Research and Development program having been signed with the Lavians, and some initiate preparation and groundwork having been done in its main military airforce bases and facilities, the military HQ of Nordiheim have sent a production order for 50 F-130 Diamondbacks to be produced for the Nordiheim air force to the Ijesa Dynamics company together with a contract request for logistical and technical support to get everything up and going as fast as possible for when the aircrafts fully arrive.

If the F-130 can be integrated and used by the air force as well as is hoped and expected then it will most likely not be the last order sent to the Lavian company.

[b]Request for testing permission[/b]

A request for testing cooperation and landing permission on a Lavian carrier have also been sent to the Lavian military to gain the ability to perform live carrier landing and take-off tests to aid in the final developing phase of the KJ-8AC.
The reason for this request is that since Nordiheim does not have carriers of its own at this point in time it can not perform these tests itself which could unnecessarily delay the development of the aircraft.
In addition it can also help both parties to gain some hands-on experience with the aircraft and preemptively discover anything that could be advantageous to change or add on the aircraft for the Lavian navy at an early stage.
If everything goes well it is hoped that the KJ-8AC might enter production as early as late 2028 or early 2029.
[/spoiler]

[b]The Navy transfers its F-130s in trade for KJ-8As[/b]

While Ijesa Dynamics works to up production and fulfill Nordiheims recent order of the aircraft, Lavias own military has recently placed an order of 120 KJ-8A Black Swan planes, and the navy is hoping to get their hands on them before the airforce. While not confirmed, it is rumored that the Navy has specifically negotiated with Nordheim to fulfill 24 aircraft in their order with the ones the navy has already been operating. This would allow technicians, pilots, and other military staff at the NAF to get a full look at the aircraft and test how it functions much earlier than they would be able to otherwise. In turn, the navy asks to get 24 KJ-8As, enough to fully supply a squadron on two of Lavias three carriers. 

[b]KJ-8AC tests on Lavian carrier[/b]

Over the last week, the KJ-8AC has reportedly been conducting carrier landing trials near Makinar and New Westmore. This doesnt come as a surprise as while Nordiheim is debating on building fleet carriers, they lack such at this time, and Lavia is available and willing to help in such tests. The KJ-8AC prototype embarked its first long-haul flight, passing from Nordiheim, over the USO, and finally landing on Eoman Island in the Yumar Island Chain. The aircraft refueled and continued to a naval airbase on Makinar, where its maintenance crew was flown along with space parts aboard a multitude of cargo aircraft. After a few mock trials on the airbase to ensure that its arrestor hook was ready for a carrier landing, it completed its first carrier landing and takeoff on March 16th, 2028. This not only brought celebration from both nations and the mixed crew aboard the carrier, but shows the growing possibility for the KJ-8AC to reach production by late 2028.
